text:
Brayden Point came off injured reserve on Nov. 17 and picked up an assist in his first game back, and Tampa won two of the three since. When he plays, the Lightning control the ice: 56% of the shot attempts and 60% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, at five on five, five points better than without him.

He has 18 points in 20 games, but the goal column is light. Five goals on 7.9 expected, shooting 11.4% against a career that's been much better than that. He keeps getting to the looks, and goals tend to follow chances.

One caution from Evolving-Hockey on last season: his results ran well ahead of his chances (2.4 wins against 0.7 expected), and he plays with teammates whose impact ranks in the 96th percentile, which flatters his raw on-ice numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 67% of his entries. Watch the shooting: with full health and those chances, the goals should come in bunches.
